items.t: Bacterial skin infections such as impetigo, folliculitis and furunculosis (active against Staphylococcus aureus including MRSA, and streptococci).

src.q: Bactroban Ointment is used for skin infections, e.g. impetigo, folliculitis, furunculosis.
including methicillin-resistant strains, other staphylococci, streptococci

items.t: Clearing nasal carriage of staphylococci, including MRSA.

src.q: The elimination of nasal carriage of staphylococci, including methicillin resistant

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the two UK mupirocin SmPCs (ointment, nasal ointment) or the SPS breastfeeding page accessed.

items.t: Adults (including elderly and hepatic impairment) and children: apply 2 to 3 times a day for up to 10 days, depending on response. Discard any product left at the end of treatment.

src.q: Two to three times a day for up to ten days, depending on the response.
Any product remaining at the end of treatment should be discarded.

items.t: Adults and children: apply to the inside of each nostril 2 to 3 times a day. Nasal carriage normally clears within 5 to 7 days.

src.q: should be applied to the anterior nares two to three times a day
Nasal carriage should normally clear within 5-7 days of commencing treatment.

items.t: Children use the adult dose; no lower age limit is stated. For infants, the nasal ointment may be applied with a cotton bud.

src.q: Adults (including elderly/hepatically impaired) and children
A cotton bud may be used instead of the little finger for the application in particular to infants or patients who are very ill.

items.t: Skin ointment: not suitable for use in the eye or the nose.

src.q: This Bactroban Ointment formulation is not suitable for ophthalmic or intranasal use.

items.t: Skin ointment: polyethylene glycol can be absorbed from open wounds and damaged skin. Do not use where large amounts may be absorbed, especially in moderate or severe renal impairment.

src.q: Polyethylene glycol can be absorbed from open wounds and damaged skin and is excreted by the kidneys.
mupirocin ointment should not be used in conditions where absorption of large quantities of polyethylene glycol is possible, especially if there is evidence of moderate or severe renal impairment

items.t: Skin ointment: not for use with cannulae or at a central venous cannulation site.

src.q: use in conjunction with cannulae and
at the site of central venous cannulation

items.t: Stop if a sensitisation reaction or severe local irritation occurs; remove the product and give appropriate treatment.

src.q: Should a possible sensitisation reaction or severe local irritation occur with the use of Bactroban Ointment, treatment should be discontinued
Should a possible sensitisation reaction or severe local irritation occur with the use of Bactroban Nasal Ointment, treatment should be discontinued

items.t: Prolonged use may lead to overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Pseudomembranous colitis is possible (less likely with topical use): stop at once if prolonged or significant diarrhoea or abdominal cramps occur.

src.q: prolonged use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms
if prolonged or significant diarrhoea occurs or the patient experiences abdominal cramps, treatment should be discontinued immediately and the patient investigated further

items.t: Skin ointment: do not mix with other preparations (dilution reduces antibacterial activity and stability).

src.q: Do not mix with other preparations as there is a risk of dilution, resulting in a reduction of the antibacterial activity

items.t: No clinical experience in pregnancy; animal studies showed no harm to the fetus. Use only when the potential benefit outweighs the possible risk.

src.q: Reproduction studies on Bactroban in animals have revealed no evidence of harm to the foetus
Bactroban should only be used in pregnancy when the potential benefits outweigh the possible risks of treatment.

items.t: SPS: mupirocin can be used during breastfeeding; as a precaution, monitor the infant for rash. Avoid direct contact between the infant and the treated area.

src.q: Mupirocin can be used during breastfeeding.
As a precaution, monitor the infant for rash.
Care should be taken to avoid direct contact between the infant and impetigo lesion(s) and treated area.

items.t: SmPC: no information on excretion in milk. If a cracked nipple is treated, wash it thoroughly before breastfeeding.

src.q: There is no information on the excretion of Bactroban in milk.
If a cracked nipple is to be treated, it should be thoroughly washed prior to breast feeding.

items.t: No human fertility data; rat studies showed no effect on fertility.

src.q: There are no data on the effects of mupirocin on human fertility.
Studies in rats showed no effects on fertility

items.t: Skin ointment: common burning at the application site; uncommon itching, redness, stinging and dryness, and skin sensitisation.

src.q: Common: Burning localised to the area of application.
Uncommon: Itching, erythema, stinging and dryness localised to the area of application.

items.t: Nasal ointment: uncommon nasal mucosa reactions.

src.q: Uncommon: Nasal mucosa reactions.

items.t: Very rare systemic allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, generalised rash, urticaria and angioedema.

src.q: Systemic allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, generalised rash, urticaria and angioedema

items.t: Stop if sensitisation or severe local irritation develops.

items.t: Skin ointment: course up to 10 days; review response.

src.q: Two to three times a day for up to ten days, depending on the response.

items.t: Skin ointment: apply a small amount to cover the affected area; it may be covered with a dressing. Do not mix with other preparations.

src.q: A small quantity of Bactroban ointment should be applied to cover the affected area.
The treated area may be covered by a dressing.

items.t: Nasal ointment: put a match-head amount on the little finger, apply inside each nostril, then press the sides of the nose together to spread it.

src.q: A small amount of the ointment about the size of a match head is placed on the little finger and applied to the inside of each nostril.
The nostrils are closed by pressing the sides of the nose together

items.t: Avoid contact with the eyes; if it gets into the eyes, rinse well with water.

src.q: Avoid contact with the eyes.
If contaminated, the eyes should be thoroughly irrigated with water until the ointment residues have been removed.
